title: PCP Protocol Schema
description: This top-level schema is a $defs container, not a single message shape -- PCP has many message types (see $defs above), each validated individually. A per-message-type JSON-RPC method registry (mapping method name -> request/response $ref pairs) is the next artifact needed here, not yet written -- see docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 11 open items.

LeaseState.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 6. PENDING exists because Raft arbitration takes time -- this is not instantaneous.

RobotState.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 5. SAFE is sticky -- no path back to ACTIVE except through the full recovery handshake (sec 10.7 / RecoveryPhase below).

RecoveryPhase.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.7. Only present while robotState transitions out of SAFE. Verified against docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md's TLA+ model, formal/PMCPRecovery.tla -- these five phases are a real sequence, not five independently-reachable labels.

enumDescriptions.1: Controlled deceleration, then power removal (watchdog/gate failure/lease expiry)

ErrorCode.description: Superset of pmcp/types.py's 10 base codes and v05/pmcp_v5_types.py's 5 robotics-specific additions -- these did not conflict, only differed in completeness, so both are retained here without loss.

SensorType.description: Union of pmcp/types.py's generic vocabulary and v05's robotics-specific vocabulary. Kept as one superset enum (unlike ShadowVerdict, these values don't semantically conflict -- see MIGRATION_MAP.md).

RobotIdentity.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 4 identity/attestation layer. From v05/pmcp_v5_types.py, the only source file that modeled this.

tee_attestation_quote.description: Opaque TEE attestation quote (SGX/SEV/TrustZone/DICE), base64-encoded. Null if the robot has no TEE (permitted, but such robots cannot participate in physical-locality-required leases -- see sec 10.4).

LocationProof.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.4. TEE attestation proves code integrity, not location -- this is the separate distance-bounding layer. BLE RSSI is sanity-check only, never load-bearing on its own.

uwb_distance_bound_m.description: IEEE 802.15.4z secure-ranging distance to the nearest trusted anchor, meters.

pose_signature.description: Ed25519-signed pose report (robot_id, pose, timestamp, optional fiducial_id) -- see sec 10.4. Note: commercial 802.15.4z does not achieve pure Brands-Chaum mafia-fraud resistance; treat as strong, not perfect.

ble_rssi_sanity_check.description: Advisory only. MUST NOT gate any safety decision on its own.

valid_until.description: Tight expiry window -- a moving robot's location claim must expire before it could plausibly have exited its declared zone. Anchor geometry and expiry window are deployment-specific (sec 10.4, still open).

SpatialLeaseReservation.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.5. R*-tree reservation tuple, query AABB inflated by safety_margin before intersection check.

aabb.description: Axis-aligned bounding box, meters, in the zone's reference frame.

safety_margin_m.description: Must be >= v_max * T_safe + sensor_uncertainty_r (sec 10.5 formula). Not auto-derivable from this schema alone -- see sec 11 open items.

priority_class.description: ESTOP reservations override any existing reservation regardless of time/space overlap.

raft_leader_id.description: Only the Raft-elected leader for this zone may grant an ACTIVE lease (sec 6). Null if state is not ACTIVE/PENDING.

granted_at.description: Unix timestamp, seconds since epoch (matches time.time() in all reference SDKs).

expires_at.description: Unix timestamp, seconds since epoch (matches time.time() in all reference SDKs).

heartbeat_interval_ms.description: Missed heartbeat -> Safe State, independent of expires_at (sec 3 invariant 6).

fence_token.description: Monotonically increasing fencing token (Kleppmann 2016). MUST be re-presented on every actuation call against this zone, not only at lease-request time -- catches the paused-holder/stale-view failure mode even when lease_id still lexically matches. Current reference SDKs use a single-process monotonic counter; Raft-backed multi-replica deployments should use the Raft term number as the source (see raft_leader_id).

ConstitutionCheck.description: From pmcp/types.py -- carried forward as-is, not present in v05.

ConformalConfidence.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.2. Part of ShadowResult -- never a bare boolean.

DeterminismBlock.description: sec 10.8 -- ensemble_disagreement and this block feed the empirical epsilon_max determination; not derivable from schema alone.

hardware_fingerprint.description: Device/driver/cuDNN/precision fingerprint, for cross-hardware determinism tracking.

ShadowResult.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.1-10.2. The monitor's composite verdict, NOT the raw HNN prediction, gates actuation -- see 'verdict' description. This replaces the old, incompatible ShadowStatus enums from pmcp/sdk (lowercase) and v05 (uppercase, different members) -- see MIGRATION_MAP.md.
ShadowResult.$comment: Sec 10.2: 'Every Shadow validation response must be a typed record, not a bare boolean, minimally including: verdict, the predicted trajectory/forces/energy, a conformal-prediction confidence block, a monitoring block, and a determinism block.' All five keys are therefore REQUIRED. The three blocks are individually NULLABLE, because a subsystem that is not implemented must report that explicitly rather than omit the key -- an absent key is indistinguishable from a bare-boolean verdict, which is the exact anti-pattern sec 10.2 forbids. The previous 'required: [verdict]' let {"verdict": "PASS", "predicted_trajectory": {}} validate cleanly, which is a safety-relevant hole: a Shadow gate that reports only a verdict is the bare-boolean case, and it would have passed the schema.

verdict.description: Set by the non-ML monitor (sec 10.1), not the HNN directly. FAIL = hard limit violated. INDETERMINATE = confidence/OOD/ensemble check exceeded threshold ('I don't know' != 'it's fine'). Both FAIL and INDETERMINATE block actuation.

predicted_trajectory.description: Robot-class-specific predicted trajectory/forces/energy. Left open (additionalProperties) deliberately -- see pcp-servers per-robot-class schemas for concrete shapes. Optional/nullable: physics or geometric simulators may predict a single resulting pose rather than a full trajectory; report that honestly as null here rather than fabricate trajectory samples.

confidence.description: Optional/nullable. Requires the HNN-Simplex monitor's conformal-prediction calibration -- an open research item (see pcp-spec docs/research), not implemented in any reference SDK as of this version. Do not populate with fabricated values.

monitoring.description: Optional/nullable. Requires the HNN ensemble-disagreement/OOD monitor -- not implemented in any reference SDK as of this version. Do not populate with fabricated values.

determinism.description: Optional/nullable. Requires cross-hardware determinism budget measurement -- an open research item (see pcp-spec docs/research), not implemented in any reference SDK as of this version. Do not populate with fabricated values.

status.description: Reference-SDK diagnostic status from the physics/geometric simulator (e.g. safe/collision/floor_guard/speed_limit). More granular than verdict; verdict is derived from this.

predicted_pose.description: Single predicted resulting pose {x,y,z,...} from the physics/geometric simulator.

AuditEventType.description: From pmcp/types.py -- carried forward, not present in v05.

MetricsSnapshot.description: From pmcp/types.py -- carried forward, not present in v05.

BatchActuationRequest.description: From pmcp/types.py -- carried forward, not present in v05. Note: sec 3 invariant 7 (SingleActuationPerLease) means batching needs an explicit design, not implicit concurrency -- this schema does not yet resolve how batch items relate to the single-actuation-per-lease invariant. Flagged for follow-up, not resolved here.

EStopMessage.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 2, 3 (Inv 5), 4. First-class, lease-independent, bypasses Lease->Constitution->Shadow entirely. NOT modeled as an ErrorCode -- this is a distinct message type precisely so it cannot inherit the gate pipeline's latency/failure modes.

triggered_at.description: Unix timestamp, seconds since epoch (matches time.time() in all reference SDKs).

stop_category.description: E-Stop is always Stop Category 0 (immediate, uncontrolled power removal) -- sec 4 table.

JWSProtectedHeader.description: docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md sec 10.6. JWS (RFC 7515) w/ EdDSA (RFC 8037), signing over RFC 8785 canonical JSON. nonce + timestamp are mandatory for safety-critical messages -- without them a captured command is trivially replayable.

SignedMessageEnvelope.description: Wraps any safety-critical JSON-RPC 2.0 payload. Verifier MUST reject anything outside the replay window or with a reused (kid, nonce) pair (sec 10.6).

payload.description: The JSON-RPC 2.0 request/response/notification object, canonicalized per RFC 8785 before signing.

$comment.const: This schema intentionally has no top-level 'properties' beyond this comment -- see 'description' above.
